title: alternating-analytic-counterexample, explained
h1: Precomposition on continuous alternating maps is not analytic in characteristic 2: a Lean 4 counterexample
lead: The tempting statement “f ↦ m ∘ (f, …, f) on continuous alternating maps is Cω (analytic) for every normed field” is false. Over an explicitly constructed complete, non-archimedean field of characteristic 2, with E = ℓ∞ and 2-forms, the map is not even analytic at 0. The Lean files contain complete-looking proofs with no sorry outside the deliberate placeholders in Challenge.lean. The Lean was not built for this site.
desc: An unofficial plain-English tour of Jack McCarthy's Lean 4 + Mathlib counterexample: precomposition on continuous alternating 2-forms on ℓ^∞ is not analytic over a non-spherically-complete field of characteristic 2. The proof runs through a bilinear lift, a characteristic-2 determinant identity summed over a hypercube, a gliding-hump tail lemma, and a hand-built Puiseux-series field.
startNote: Start with the headline, then the map Q and its target space F. The proof has three independent parts. (1) Analysis: not_analyticAt_Q turns analyticity into a bilinear lift and then into a family that core_false shows cannot exist. (2) Algebra: the finite lemma and its hypercube sum. (3) The field: exists_field, built from 2-power Puiseux series.
sizeNote: About 4,470 lines of Lean in 21 files (18 under AltCounter/, plus AltCounter.lean, Challenge.lean and Solution.lean), with a paper and the original notes in paper/.
agentCtx: A Lean 4 + Mathlib counterexample: assuming Mathlib's ContinuousAlternatingMap.compContinuousLinearMapCLM is C^ω for all normed spaces over all nontrivially normed fields derives False, via ℓ^∞ 2-forms over a completed 2-power Puiseux series field of characteristic 2.

gloss.NontriviallyNormedField: A field with an absolute value ‖·‖ that is not trivial: some element has ‖x‖ > 1. Examples include ℝ, ℂ, ℚ_p, and the field built here.
gloss.NormedField: A field with a multiplicative absolute value ‖·‖ satisfying the triangle inequality.
gloss.NormedAddCommGroup: An additive group with a norm ‖·‖ that induces its metric.
gloss.NormedSpace: NormedSpace 𝕜 E: E is a vector space over the normed field 𝕜 with ‖c • x‖ ≤ ‖c‖ ‖x‖.
gloss.Fintype: Fintype ι: ι is a finite type whose elements can be listed. Here ι indexes the arguments of an alternating map.
gloss.ContDiff: ContDiff 𝕜 n f: f is n times continuously differentiable. With n = ω (written ⊤ : WithTop ℕ∞), it means f is analytic, i.e. given locally by convergent power series.
gloss.AnalyticAt: AnalyticAt 𝕜 f x: near x, f equals the sum of a convergent power series of continuous multilinear maps.
gloss.ContinuousAlternatingMap.compContinuousL: Precomposition: for a continuous linear f : E → E′, the continuous linear map that sends an alternating form m on E′ to m ∘ (f, …, f) on E.
gloss.IsUltrametricDist: The strong triangle inequality: dist(x, z) ≤ max(dist(x, y), dist(y, z)). For a field, ‖x + y‖ ≤ max(‖x‖, ‖y‖) (non-archimedean).
gloss.Fin: Fin n: the numbers 0, …, n − 1. Here Fin 2 means alternating maps of two arguments.
gloss.False: The false proposition. Proving False from a hypothesis refutes that hypothesis.
gloss.StrictAnti: A strictly decreasing function: m < n implies r(m) > r(n).
gloss.Submodule: A linear subspace of a module (vector space).
gloss.Submodule.span: The smallest subspace containing a given set: all finite linear combinations of its elements.
gloss.Set.range: The set of all values of a function.
